hook: A very short file about a cockatoo that writes like a young child. There is nothing violent in it; the weight comes entirely from a few handwritten notes. Read it slowly and pay attention to the spelling, which is preserved on purpose.
whyItMatters: SCP-1192 shows how little an SCP article needs in order to affect people: one exchange, one researcher note, and a handful of misspelled lines. It belongs to the wiki's quieter, sadder strand, where the anomaly is someone's situation rather than a threat. Its length makes it easy to recommend to readers who want something that lingers more than it shocks.
thingsToNotice:
Look at the containment procedures: pencils and paper are listed as a requirement, which tells you how the Foundation has chosen to treat the subject. The researcher keeps a professional distance, yet the closing note slips into a slightly warmer first-person voice.

The list of drawings and pages is arranged so that each item hits a little harder than the one before. The sign-off from a senior observer leaves it feeling like a case file nobody quite knows how to close.

related.note: A much darker story about minds unable to act freely.
A far lighter take on an anomaly defined by its need for attachment.
